Helix to run 50k token/day synthetic run with seed traffic and report error rates (target date 2026-11-03)
SE to provide recommended retry/backoff settings + sample client snippet (by 2026-10-31)

action_items: Luca (Redwood SE): collect node-level traces and KV cache hit-rate breakdown; due 2026-10-30
Priya (Redwood Support): export 502/503 sample payloads and put on shared drive; due 2026-10-30

summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recurring 5xx spikes and timeouts during traffic bursts. Team agreed to run targeted synthetic tests, extract traces and kvcache metrics, and try a conservative exponential backoff + jitter in the client. Redwood will provide recommended retry snippets and upload logs for triage.
topics: retry budget and exponential backoff with jitter
kv cache hit/miss impact on tail latency
fallback routing and model variant rollbacks
transcript:
00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, quick roll call?
00:08 - Ravi (Helix): hey, Ravi here, platform.
00:11 - Aisha (Helix): Aisha, backend.
00:13 - Tom (Helix): Tom, SRE.
00:15 - Natalie (Helix): Natalie joining.
00:17 - Luca (Redwood SE): Luca on the call. Priya's watching the logs and will upload after.
00:22 - Maya: goal today is to validate the mitigations from last week - specifically backoff tuning and whether prefix/KV cache changes helped the tail. also want to assign lab work.
00:35 - Tom: quick update from our side, after the burst last thurs we saw 502/503s concentrated between 11:30 and 11:45 PST, about a 4% error rate at peak. baseline normally <0.2.
00:50 - Aisha: yeah the request pattern was a sharp double spike, we had a batch job and some user traffic. i throttled a couple of internal queues but errors persisted.
01:05 - Luca: from the Redwood telemetry, we saw slot exhaustion on a small subset of nodes — the concurrent sequence length for those requests was higher, k-v cache cold misses increased. some of the 5xx correlate with long model compile times for a rare path.
01:22 - Ravi: when you say slot exhaustion, is that queuing overflow or OOM?
01:26 - Luca: more like request queue backpressure, not OOM, queue timeouts eventually triggered 504s then cascaded. we did see a handful of 502s where the runtime aborted because a dependent kernel timed out under contention.
01:44 - Maya: ok that's useful. so two levers: reduce client retries to avoid thundering herd, and improve the server-side admission/queueing.
01:56 - Tom: on admission control, we tried to flatten incoming spikes with a rolling window on our side, but the window we used (200ms) might be too small and created microbursts.
02:11 - Aisha: can you explain the windowing idea again, the rolling window? i might be misremembering.
02:16 - Tom: sure — we mean we cap rps over a 1s sliding window, but we implemented it as 200ms buckets which ended up bunching when clock alignment happened.
02:28 - Priya (Redwood Support): note: the telemetry shows that kv cache hit-rate drops from ~88% to ~42% during the spike windows. that increases token compute per request.
02:40 - Natalie: interesting, so cold KV misses amplify compute per request and makes the nodes slower -> longer queue latency -> more timeouts.
02:49 - Luca: exactly. also we found a handful of requests with long prompt prefixes—those bypassed prefix caching due to slightly different whitespace, so small prompt normalization might improve cache hits.
03:05 - Maya: that is a good quick win — normalize whitespace and common metadata fields at the client.
03:15 - Tom: on retries, we currently have clients retry 3 times with fixed 500ms intervals. that probably worsened the crowding.
03:24 - Aisha: what's the guidance — exponential backoff? full jitter?
03:27 - Luca: recommend exponential backoff with full jitter (per AWS Best Practices). starting base 100ms, multiplier 2, cap 2s, max attempts 4, but importantly add a retry budget so the client stops retrying if overall system load high.
03:46 - Ravi: can you define retry budget?
03:48 - Luca: simple approach: allow X retries per minute per API key; or use a token-bucket on client side that refills slowly. Redwood also supports server-side 429 hints that include retry-after and capacity signals, we can surface those.
04:04 - Maya: do we have a short code snippet we can drop in?
04:07 - Luca: yes i'll attach examples after the call. i'll also include sample logic for honoring 429s and backoff budgets.
04:16 - Tom: for server-side fixes, what are the knobs? is it autoscale threshold, queue depth, or smarter routing?
04:23 - Luca: all of the above. quick mitigation is to increase queue depth and add a fast-path for cached prefixes. medium-term is to tune kernel scheduling and pre-warm model instances for the high-seq-length paths.
04:37 - Maya: the team asked about fallback routing — if a model variant fails, can we route to a cheaper/older variant automatically?
04:45 - Luca: yes, Redwood supports automatic fallback to compatible variants. we can configure a canary and automatic fallback policy so traffic reroutes when error thresholds exceed X for Y seconds.
04:56 - Aisha: is there a cost impact to fallback?
04:58 - Luca: very slightly; older variants may be smaller and cheaper but could have quality regressions. we'll provide tradeoff metrics.
05:08 - Ravi: security ask — we need audit logs for these incidents for compliance, and a SOC2 addendum.
05:15 - Maya: we will share SOC2 docs and the audit log export process. Priya will drop the link.
05:21 - Priya: uploading now: redwood.com/soc2-addendum (note: this is demo link). also SSO/SAML checklist will be attached.
05:34 - Tom: any quick wins to reduce 5xx this week?
05:37 - Luca: normalization to improve KV hit-rate, client-side backoff changes, and a temporary increase of concurrency limit for critical routes during the scheduled synthetic run.
05:47 - Aisha: for the synthetic run, we can simulate three burst profiles: short sharp, double hump, and sustained ramp. we'll do short sharp tomorrow.
05:58 - Maya: ok set expectation — run short sharp, capture traces, and then we'll correlate.
06:06 - Natalie: can we also keep sampling of user requests to check for prompt variation that breaks caching?
06:11 - Luca: yes add a sampling hook, we recommend 1% sample of full payloads (PII redaction configured).
06:20 - Tom: quick question — we saw some 5xxs at 40s mark in the trace, but our client timeout is 60s; is the runtime retrying internally?
06:28 - Luca: runtime doesn't retry opaque requests; those 40s marks look like subcomponent kernel timeouts that surfaced as 502s. that is why we need span traces to identify which kernel.
06:40 - Maya: timeline recap and owners? we'll need logs by tomorrow so Luca/Priya can triage.
06:46 - Ravi: yep we'll enable extended logs for 72 hours starting now. Tom will send ids to Redwood.
06:53 - Aisha: on the sample payloads, how should we redact PHI?
06:58 - Priya: please replace patient-specific tokens with placeholders, we can verify redaction before upload.
07:05 - Tom: note: also checking network egress, but nothing changed in infra last week. i'll still share security group rules.
07:13 - Luca: great. next, small UX question: is there a way for Redwood to surface per-key retry-budget usage in console?
07:20 - Maya: currently we have per-route token usage; exposing retry budget usage is on the product backlog but we can surface a temporary metric via tracing.
07:30 - Natalie: last thing — we have a compliance review next Wed, could we get the audit timeline?
07:35 - Maya: we'll send the SOC2 addendum and an audit export step-by-step within 48 hours.
07:42 - Ravi: ok sounds good.
07:44 - Maya: anything else from Helix?
07:46 - Aisha: no, that covers it.
07:48 - Tom: no.
07:49 - Luca: quick plug — i'll push a recommended retry snippet and a small normalization lib to the shared drive after this.
07:55 - Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the log run, i'll propose a 30-minute slot.
07:59 - meeting end

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts: "kayvee cache" appears in some auto notes where speaker said KV cache and some acronyms like SAML were transcribed as "SAMEL" in auto-captions.
